name: Seven Hills to World Power: Rome's Rise and Fall
description: A village on the Tiber becomes the master of the Mediterranean, then loses the West. Generals, emperors, roads, arenas and the faith that outlasted them.

checkpoints.name: A village on the Tiber
checkpoints.note: Tradition says Rome began in 753 BCE. A market place that became the Roman Forum, a Latin tongue and a set of old gods grew into a town ruled by kings who were later expelled.

checkpoints.name: The Republic and the Punic Wars
checkpoints.note: Rome wrote the Twelve Tables, built the Appian Way and fought Carthage three times. Hannibal won at Cannae, but Scipio Africanus beat him at Zama, and Roman concrete soon shaped a bigger city.

checkpoints.name: Strongmen and civil war
checkpoints.note: Rich generals ruled the provinces and the poor wanted land. Spartacus led a slave revolt, Julius Caesar won Gaul and then the civil war, and his heir Augustus ended the Republic.

checkpoints.name: Emperors and the Roman peace
checkpoints.note: Under Augustus the Roman Empire began and Pax Romana followed. Virgil wrote the Aeneid, Vesuvius buried Pompeii, and Trajan, Hadrian and Marcus Aurelius ruled while the Colosseum, Pantheon and Hadrian's Wall went up.

checkpoints.name: Crisis, faith and fall
checkpoints.note: Civil wars and invaders strained the state. Diocletian divided power, Constantine turned to Christianity and the Edict of Milan, and after Attila's raids and the sack of Rome the West ended in 476.
